inputs.content:
# Palisade Docs: raise prices while churn is rising? — briefing pack

> **Synthetic benchmark data.** The company, people, competitors and every figure in this pack are fictional. They were generated for a reasoning benchmark and are internally consistent, but they are not real market data.

## 1. Context

Palisade Docs sells document-workflow and e-signature software. ARR is $86.0M from 7,400
customers in three segments. Monthly customer churn has risen over the past year, and the CFO wants a price increase.

**Decision maker:** CEO Ravi Menon, deciding on the 2027 pricing plan with the leadership team in December 2026.

## 2. Decision question

**Should Palisade raise prices in 2027 while customer churn is rising, and if so, how?**

## 3. Objectives and constraints

- Grow ARR at least 15% in 2027 (from $86.0M).
- Keep net revenue retention above 100% overall.
- Price changes apply at renewal; enterprise contracts follow their own terms.

## 4. Current views inside the company

- **CFO:** "Raise list prices 12% on every plan at renewal from January 2027. That is $10.3M of ARR. Churn is an
  onboarding problem, not a price problem."
- **CEO's concern:** "Churn is going up. A price rise now could push it higher."
- **Head of Customer Success:** "The 2025 promotion brought in customers who never set the product up."

## 5. Segments

**Table 1. Segments, mid-2026**

| Segment | Customers | ARR, $M | Monthly logo churn H1 2025 | Monthly logo churn H1 2026 | Net revenue retention (trailing 12 months) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SMB | 5,900 | 21.0 | 2.0% | 3.1% | 94% |
| Mid-market | 1,350 | 41.0 | 0.6% | 0.8% | 112% |
| Enterprise | 150 | 24.0 | 0.2% | 0.2% | 118% |

SMB = 1–50 employees, self-serve, monthly or annual plans. Mid-market = 51–1,000 employees, annual contracts.
Enterprise = over 1,000 employees, mostly multi-year contracts.

## 6. The 2025 SMB promotion

- From February to August 2025, new self-serve SMB customers got 50% off for their first six months. The
  promotion brought in 2,100 SMB customers who are still counted in the base above (about $4.4M of ARR at full price).
- Share of new customers who sent at least five documents in their first month: 41% for the promotion cohort,
  72% for other cohorts.
- Monthly churn in H1 2026 for SMB customers who did **not** come through the promotion: 2.1% (H1 2025 for the
  same kind of customers: 2.0%).

**Table 2. Main churn reason "price / found a cheaper option", share of churned customers who answered the exit survey**

| Group | Share citing price |
|---|---|
| all SMB churners H1 2025 | 19% |
| all SMB churners H1 2026 | 34% |
| promo-cohort churners H1 2026 | 52% |
| non-promo SMB churners H1 2026 | 18% |

Most promotion-cohort customers who left did so within two months of the discount ending.

## 7. Competitor

- **Inkwell** launched a Starter plan at $9 per user per month in October 2025. Palisade's SMB plan is $15 per
  user per month; Business plan $29; Inkwell Pro $24.
- Palisade's win rate in SMB deals where Inkwell was considered fell from 51% (H1 2025) to 38% (H1 2026).
  Inkwell has not been seen in mid-market or enterprise deals with more than 200 seats.

## 8. Pricing history and tests

- **2023 SMB price increase:** +8% at renewal. SMB monthly churn rose from 1.8% to 2.3% for six months, then
  settled at 1.9%.
- **2024 mid-market test:** +10% list price for new mid-market sign-ups for three months: conversion 23.1%
  against 23.6% for the control group (difference not statistically significant).
- **Enterprise:** 60% of enterprise ARR is under contracts that cap annual price increases at 7%. 40% of
  enterprise ARR renews in 2027, as does 85% of mid-market ARR and all SMB ARR.

## 9. Product and customer evidence

- Mid-market and enterprise customers rate Palisade's integrations and audit trail as the main reasons they stay
  (customer advisory board, 2026).
- SMB customers who send fewer than five documents in their first month churn at about three times the rate of
  those who send more.

## 10. Other material

- **Board dashboard (Q2 2026):** "Monthly churn: 1.4% → 2.3%." The dashboard does not define the measure.
- **Head of Customer Success:** "An onboarding programme will halve SMB churn within two quarters."

## 11. Uncertainties

- How price-sensitive non-promotion SMB customers are now that Inkwell exists.
- Whether the promotion cohort can be activated, or will mostly churn regardless.
- Whether the mid-market test (new sign-ups) predicts how existing customers react at renewal.

storyline.governing_thought: Raise 2027 renewal prices 10% in mid-market, 7% in enterprise and 8% in other SMB, and hold the 2025 promotion cohort while it is onboarded

exec_summary.text: Churn is rising because of customers the 2025 SMB promotion brought in

sub_points.text: SMB holds 80% of customers but only 24% of ARR, and only its churn jumped
The promotion cohort is 36% of SMB customers but 56% of those who leave

exec_summary.text: Customers outside the promotion can take a rise; SMB carries the most Inkwell risk

sub_points.text: Mid-market and enterprise hold 76% of ARR and keep 112% and 118% of revenue
Inkwell's $9 plan cut SMB win rates from 51% to 38%; other SMB churn barely moved

exec_summary.text: The CFO's 12% is worth $7.6M, not $10.3M; a segmented rise adds $5.5M before churn

sub_points.text: Only $65.5M of ARR renews in 2027, and 60% of enterprise ARR is capped at 7%
Each step rests on a test, a precedent or a cap; the promotion cohort is held
The 15% target is reached only if existing customers keep today's 109% retention

exec_summary.text: Reprice from January with an SMB control group, onboard the cohort, stop if churn spikes

sub_points.text: Mid-market 10%, enterprise 7%, other SMB 8%; no rise for the promotion cohort
A March read-out stops the SMB rise if churn runs above the 2023 reaction

next_steps.action: Approve mid-market +10% and enterprise +7% at 2027 renewals and send renewal notices
Set up the other-SMB +8% rise with a random control group kept at today's price
next_steps.owner: CFO with Head of Customer Success

next_steps.action: Run the onboarding push for promotion-cohort accounts; no price change for them in 2027
Replace the dashboard churn figure with logo and ARR churn by segment and cohort
March read-out: continue or pause the SMB rise against the stop rules

body.assumptions_header: The ceiling assumes full activation; the evidence supports less
assumptions: Ceiling: the cohort's churn falls from 4.9% a month to the 2.1% of other SMB customers from January
Activation explains only part of the gap: low users churn about three times as fast, so 41% activation predicts 2.9%, not 4.9%
If the rest is a lasting reaction to the discount ending, full activation cuts churn to 3.3% and keeps about $0.5M
Halving SMB churn, as proposed, means 1.55% a month, below the 2.1% of SMB customers the promotion never touched
The briefing pack gives no programme cost; logo churn is applied to the cohort's ARR

footnotes: Estimate by the team from the briefing pack; live formulas are in the Calculations sheet of the source workbook

lead_message.text: A March read-out and two stop rules let Palisade reverse course before churn costs more than the rise earns

slides.rationale: Moves, gates and stop rules over 2027 -> timeline
slides.unit_line: **2027 pricing roadmap**, by customer group, December 2026 to end of 2027

bars.label: Continue only if the read-out clears

slides.so_what: Stop rules: pause SMB if repriced churn runs 0.5 percentage points above the control group, the 2023 peak; pause mid-market above 1.6% a month

constraints.item: Grow ARR at least 15% in 2027, to $98.9M
constraints.effect: reached only if trailing NRR of 109% holds: the bridge then leaves $0.1M for new customers, $1.5M if mid-market reacts like SMB did in 2023; the title says 'only if'

constraints.item: Keep net revenue retention above 100% overall
constraints.effect: plan lifts NRR to about 115%; overall NRR would drop below 100% only if mid-market NRR fell from 112% to about 93%

constraints.item: Price changes apply only at renewal; only $65.5M of ARR renews in 2027
constraints.effect: cuts the CFO's $10.3M to $7.6M and sizes every recommended step on renewing ARR

constraints.item: Enterprise contracts cap annual increases at 7% on 60% of enterprise ARR
constraints.effect: enterprise step set at 7% for all renewals; the CFO sizing assumes 60% of renewing enterprise ARR is capped

constraints.item: Churn reaction of mid-market and enterprise customers to the rise
constraints.effect: their $4.2M is gross; titles and exec item say 'before churn'; the bridge sidebar shows the case where mid-market reacts like SMB in 2023 (new customers must then bring $1.5M) and the break-even is shown on the mid-market page

constraints.item: Onboarding programme cost (not in the briefing pack)
constraints.effect: the $1.0M onboarding ceiling is before programme cost; the slide says so and gives a $0.5M low case

constraints.item: Trailing NRR may include past enterprise escalators and the promotion step-up from 50% off
constraints.effect: the growth bridge could double count part of the enterprise rise; footnoted on the retention and bridge pages

alternatives.option: CFO: raise every plan 12% at renewal from January 2027
alternatives.why: worth $7.6M, not $10.3M; the extra $2.1M over the recommendation rests on steps beyond any test, precedent or cap, a third of the total sits in SMB and part in the price-sensitive promotion cohort

alternatives.option: Raise SMB customers outside the promotion 8% from January and hold only the promotion cohort (red-team alternative to the first draft, which held all SMB until a June test)
alternatives.why: their churn is flat (2.1% against 2.0%) and price-citing is flat (18% against 19%) even after Inkwell; at the 2023 reaction it nets about $0.7M and closes most of the gap to the growth target; risk is handled with a control group and a March read-out

alternatives.option: Hold all prices in 2027 until churn is under control (the CEO's concern)
alternatives.why: churn is rising only in the promotion cohort; holding gives up $4.2M in mid-market and enterprise, where churn is low and NRR is above 110%
about $0.9M more than 10% and 7%, but above the step tested in 2024 and above the enterprise cap; the evidence cannot test it, so it is not shown as a separate row

failure_threshold.driver: Churn reaction of repriced customers, and existing-customer NRR for the growth target
failure_threshold.threshold: The mid-market rise stops paying if repriced accounts churn above about 1.6% a month (twice today's 0.8%); the other-SMB rise stops paying if it loses more than 7.4% of its ARR, about twice the 2023 reaction; the growth target needs new-customer ARR of $0.1M plus $0.86M for every percentage point NRR falls below 109%
failure_threshold.range: Pricing ARR in 2027: low $3.5M (mid-market reacts like SMB in 2023, other SMB nets $0.7M) / base $4.8M (no mid-market or enterprise reaction, other SMB net) / high $5.5M (no reaction anywhere)

consistency.headline: Raise 2027 renewal prices by segment, 10% in mid-market, 7% in enterprise and 8% for SMB outside the 2025 promotion, and hold the promotion cohort while it is onboarded
consistency.fix: Draft held all SMB until a June test; changed to an 8% January rise for other SMB with a control group after the audit. Exec item 3 says 'before churn' and the growth-target title says 'only if' NRR holds.
